So I'm going to enroll at Marshall University and study biotechnology. I was just wondering if there was anyone here who could tell me what it's actually like studying it and practicing it as your job. Also what the job market is like and what cores of science I will really be studying to do it. The job market is terrible unless you want to live in Boston or Los Angeles. Study biology, (genomics/genetics), chemistry (biochemisty), and computer science. Do not expect a job actually doing real biotechnolocial work unless you are going for your PhD. Do not even bother if you cannot get into a top 10 school. Most people have this terrible idea they they are researching the cure to cancer, you are researching a potential mutation that leads to cancer of the thyroid type 1.2adfd (made up disease). If you really, really, want to go into science then biotechnology is a good field to go into but expect terrible pay, terrible job opportunities, massive education costs, extreme nepotism, and extreme unsatisfaction in your ideas of research verse reality.
